paper.title: Online Learning with Probing for Sequential User-Centric Selection

settings.name_in_paper: Online PUCS (Probing-augmented User-Centric Selection), unknown distributions
unmapped: Each round the learner first probes up to I of M arms (observing their resource D_{t,m} and rewards R_{t,m,k} for all plays), then assigns K plays to M arms; multiple plays may share an arm
Each arm has a random resource D_{t,m} in {1,...,D_max} limiting how many plays receive reward; resources and rewards both unknown
Probing overhead: total reward multiplied by (1 - alpha(|S_t|)) for a known non-decreasing alpha
The learner knows the probing budget I, the overhead function alpha and the support bound D_max
Reward depends on full reward distributions (CDFs), not only means
settings.definition_quote: In each time slot, the decision maker first probes a subset of arms $S_t\subseteq [M]$ and based on the values of $N_{t,m}$ and $\bX_{t,m}$, $\forall~m\in S_t$, the decision maker assigns $K$ plays to $M$ arms and each play gets a reward if it receives one unit of resource from the assigned arm. ... our objective is to achieve sublinear \(\zeta\)-approximation regret ... $\mathcal{R}_{\text{regret}}(\zeta,T) = \sum_{t=1}^{T} \zeta R(S^*_t) - \sum_{t=1}^{T} R(S_t)$

unmapped: PUCS probing-and-assignment problem; the lower bound is obtained by reduction to single-play MAB (K=1 play, no probing)
settings.definition_quote: Our more general setting (with multiple plays, resource constraints, and probing) can be reduced to the single-play multi-armed bandit problem by fixing these additional features to trivial values (e.g., $K=1$ and no probing).

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Offline stochastic optimisation with known distributions (approximation algorithm for choosing a probing set); not an interactive learning problem.
unmapped: Learner knows the full resource pmf matrix P and reward CDFs F_{m,k}
Objective is to maximise R(S) = (1-alpha(|S|)) f(S) over probing sets S
settings.definition_quote: In the offline PUCS setting, the probability mass matrix $\bP$ and the true CDF $\{F_{m,k} \}_{m\in[M],k\in[K]}$ of rewards for each arm-play pair are known. We aim to determine the optimal probing set that maximizes the expected total reward

algorithms.name: OLPA (Online Learning for Joint Probing and Assignment)

source.label: offalpha1
source.quote: Let  $S^*:= \arg\max_{S\subseteq [M]} R(S)$. Algorithm \ref{offline_greedy} outputs a subset $S^{\text {pr }}$ such that $R\left(S^{\text {pr }}\right) \geq \zeta R\left(S^{\star}\right)$ where $\zeta=\frac{e-1}{2 e-1}$.

results.notes: Approximation ratio (ALG >= zeta*OPT) of offline greedy probing; restated in appendix as Theorem 3. Complexity O(I M (MK)^3) stated in paper (sample-based estimation for general distributions).

symbols.K_plays: number of plays K assigned per round
symbols.mu_sum: sum over arms m of max_{k in C_m} mu_{m,k}

conditions: regret is zeta-approximation regret with zeta=(e-1)/(2e-1)
rewards sub-Gaussian (assumed in proof of Lemma 15)
resources supported on {1,...,D_max}, independent of rewards
tuning: confidence parameter delta in (0,1) used in confidence radius epsilon_{m,k}^{(t)}

source.label: thm: online
source.quote: The regret of Algorithm \ref{alg:online} is bound by $\mathcal{R}_{\text{regret}}(\frac{e-1}{2e-1},T) \leq \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}M  \delta \left(\ln \frac{K T} { \delta} \right)^2 +4D_{\max} K $ $\left( \sum_{m\in [M]}  \max\limits_{k\in C_m} \mu_{m,k}   \right) \sqrt{2 \ln \frac{2}{\delta}} \sqrt{T} $.

results.notes: Restated as Theorem 4 in appendix. The statement does not specify expectation vs high probability; proof uses high-probability confidence events (Lemmas 12,13,16) without accounting for failure events, and the per-round regret is defined via expected R(S). Recorded as expectation with low confidence. Noise model ambiguous (paper says 'general distributions', proof assumes sub-Gaussian; experiments use [0,1] rewards). Paper summarises as O(sqrt(T)+ln^2 T).

conditions: hard instances: Bernoulli rewards, two environments with gap Delta = c/sqrt(T), reduction to single play (K=1) and no probing

source.quote: For any online algorithm \(\mathcal{A}\), there exists a worst-case configuration of reward distributions such that: \[ \mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}_{\text{regret}}] = \Omega(\sqrt{T}). \]

results.notes: Proof is a sketch via reduction to standard MAB; unclear whether it addresses the zeta-approximation regret or standard regret, so quantity left unspecified.
